introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Given that the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ with vector equations

$l_1:\ \mathbf r=2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+s(-2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j)$ and

$l_2:\ \mathbf r=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+t(3\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)$, intersect,
incertitudes: Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, sans total par question. Le champ points de l'exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions.

7(c) : 'the angle between the lines' est ambigu (angle des vecteurs directeurs : cos = -2/racine(5) ; angle aigu entre les droites : cos = 2/racine(5)). Le corrige donne les deux et retient la valeur positive 2/racine(5) pour l'angle entre les droites.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) find the values of the parameters $s$ and $t$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the point of intersection the position vectors are equal:

$(2-2s)\mathbf i+(4+6s)\mathbf j=(3+3t)\mathbf i+(-1-3t)\mathbf j.$

Equate the coefficients of $\mathbf i$ and of $\mathbf j$:

$2-2s=3+3t\ \Rightarrow\ -2s-3t=1\quad(1)$

$4+6s=-1-3t\ \Rightarrow\ 6s+3t=-5\quad(2)$

Add (1) and (2): $4s=-4\Rightarrow s=-1.$

Substitute in (1): $2-3t=1\Rightarrow t=\dfrac13.$

Check in (2): $6(-1)+3\left(\tfrac13\right)=-6+1=-5$.

**$s=-1$ and $t=\dfrac13$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Find the position vector of the point of intersection of the lines. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute $s=-1$ in $l_1$:

$\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-(-2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j)=4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j.$

Check with $t=\tfrac13$ in $l_2$: $3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+\tfrac13(3\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)=4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j$.

**The position vector is $4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j$**, that is the point $(4,-2)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the cosine of the angle between the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The angle between the lines is found from their direction vectors $\mathbf d_1=-2\mathbf i+6\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf d_2=3\mathbf i-3\mathbf j$.

$\mathbf d_1\cdot\mathbf d_2=(-2)(3)+(6)(-3)=-6-18=-24,$

$|\mathbf d_1|=\sqrt{4+36}=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10},\qquad|\mathbf d_2|=\sqrt{9+9}=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2.$

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf d_1\cdot\mathbf d_2}{|\mathbf d_1||\mathbf d_2|}=\dfrac{-24}{6\sqrt{20}}=\dfrac{-4}{2\sqrt5}=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\approx-0.894.$

The negative sign means the two direction vectors make an obtuse angle ($\approx153.4^\circ$). The (acute) angle between the two **lines** is $180^\circ-153.4^\circ=26.6^\circ$, so

**$\cos\theta=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\approx0.894$** (the angle between the direction vectors $\mathbf d_1$ and $\mathbf d_2$ has cosine $-\dfrac2{\sqrt5}$).
